summary: The LEOSA Reform Act amends 18 U.S.C. §§ 922, 926B, 926C, and 930 to let qualified active and retired law enforcement officers carry concealed firearms (including magazines) in school zones, National Park System areas, certain low-security federal facilities, and on public or common-carrier property, while expanding acceptable firearms-qualification standards and certifications.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget authority. It solely amends criminal code provisions on firearm carrying by law enforcement officers.
No tax provisions, rate changes, credits, or revenue measures appear in the bill text.
The legislation does not address healthcare policy, insurance, public coverage, or medical regulations.

The bill directly expands the rights of qualified current and retired law enforcement officers to carry concealed firearms. It amends 18 U.S.C. § 922(q) to exempt LEOSA-covered individuals from Gun-Free School Zones Act restrictions, broadens LEOSA preemption over state and local laws (including in national parks and certain public spaces), relaxes qualification standards and documentation requirements for retired officers, and permits carry in certain federal facilities previously restricted under 18 U.S.C. § 930. These changes reduce regulatory barriers and affirm broader carry authority, aligning strongly with protecting gun rights.
No immigration, border, or visa-related content is present.

While the bill touches the Gun-Free School Zones Act, it does so only to create a narrow exemption for LEOSA-qualified officers; it contains no education funding, school policy, or curriculum measures.
